newsitem.title: USA: Frontier Natural had Louisiana dry hole.
newsitem.headline: Frontier Natural had Louisiana dry hole.

text.p: Frontier Natural Gas Corp said Monday its Schooner Prospect in Plaquemines Parish, La., has completed drilling and has proven to be a dry hole.
Frontier also said three wells have been proposed from drilling at its Starboard Project, in the fourth quarter.
The Schooner Prospect was operated by Hunt Petroleum Corp, Frontier said, adding its share of the dry hole costs is expected to be about $250,000.
The company pointed out it has previously indicated the prospect was of a high risk profile but that participation was mandated by the significant reserve potential to Frontier.

Frontier said its Starboard Project, located in Terrebonne Parish, La., has had 3-D seismic shot, processed and interpreted. One planned exploratory well was proposed by FINA Inc's Fina Oil & Chemical Co, a partner in the project, and a second has now been proposed by SCANA Corp's Scana Petroleum Resources, another project partner.
A third well, which is a proven undeveloped location, has been proposed by Frontier, the company said.
In addition to the three wells, it said, there are two other prospects currently being evaluated by the partners. Additional interpretation work may lead to further prospects.
"We realistically expect drilling on two of the three proposed wells to begin in 1997," Frontier said.
"Each exploratory well in the Starboard Project is intended to test reservoirs which, if successful, would likely require additional drilling to further develop the reserves discovered."

The company also updated litigation it filed naming Offshore Group Inc in 1994, saying the Alabama Supreme Court has now affirmed the summary judgment decision against Offshore Group's claims. Frontier said its claims against the defendant may now proceed to trial.
